absent: Multiprocessor stop ordering and synchronization beyond the local only fallback shown.
Full credential state transitions, garbage collection timing and timeout values.
Cache upcall wire format, channel protocol and userspace handling.
Transport selection, retransmission timers, congestion and error recovery.
GSS mechanism internals and cryptographic processing.
Debug facility bit assignments and runtime control.
Allocation failure handling for cache and credential paths.
Lock ordering among hash lock, queue lock and client lock.

findings.text: Two helpers define a named member group that can be handled as a unit while keeping individual members accessible. One form attaches compiler attributes to the group, the other attaches a tag type. Both forward to a common implementation.
A helper declares a trailing flexible array member of a chosen element type under a chosen name, for structures whose final member has runtime length.

The overlap helper provides two views of the same storage: a whole object of a chosen type, and an alternate structure whose initial padding matches the offset of a flexible member inside that type followed by caller supplied members. The plain form exposes the same layout without extra attributes.

Register block addressing defines three derived offsets relative to a base: the set variant is four bytes past base, the clear variant eight bytes past base, and the toggle variant twelve bytes past base.
Each routed header defines an inclusion guard macro so that repeated inclusion in one translation unit has no additional effect.
A callback type represents a per CPU stop function receiving an opaque argument and returning a status integer.
One work descriptor for CPU stop operations carries queue linkage in list, callback in fn, caller address in caller, opaque argument in arg, and completion pointer in done for synchronous waiting.

An alternate work descriptor for constrained builds carries a generic work item in work plus a callback in fn and opaque argument in arg, for execution through the system workqueue rather than a dedicated stopper.

Synchronous single CPU execution only supports the calling CPU. When the target equals the current processor the callback runs immediately and its status is returned, otherwise no callback runs and ENOENT is reported.

Asynchronous single CPU execution queues the callback for later handling only when the target equals the current processor. A mismatched target triggers a one time warning and no queuing. The queued worker retrieves its container and runs the callback.

In this configuration global stop is reduced to direct local invocation. One helper runs the callback with local interrupts masked and returns its status. Two wrappers delegate to that helper and to each other respectively. Diagnostic printing for stop state is a no operation.
Single CPU callbacks are invoked with preemption disabled, and the global helper masks local interrupts across its callback and restores the prior state afterwards.
Null authentication size estimates are four units for call credentials and two units for reply credentials.
Unix authentication limits node name length to the system UTS length, allows sixteen supplemental groups, and sizes call credentials as twenty one plus the quad rounded node name length.
Credential input for authentication lookup carries a system credential reference in cred and an optional machine principal string in principal.

A cached credential object carries hash linkage in cr_hash, LRU linkage in cr_lru, deferred free linkage in cr_rcu, owning authenticator in cr_auth, operation vector in cr_ops, expiry instant in cr_expire, flag word in cr_flags, reference count in cr_count and base credential in cr_cred, with flavor specific trailing data.
Credential flag positions are zero for new, one for update, two for hashed and three for negative.

An authenticator object carries call estimate in au_cslack, reply estimate in au_rslack, verifier size in au_verfsize, alignment in au_ralign, flags in au_flags, operations in au_ops, pseudoflavor in au_flavor, reference count in au_count and cache in au_credcache, with flavor specific trailing data.

Authenticator hints use value one for data touch and value two for slack update. Credential lookup modes use value one for accepting uninitialized entries and value two for nonblocking memory behavior.
Authenticator creation parameters carry a pseudoflavor in pseudoflavor and an optional target name in target_name.

Authenticator operations comprise owner, flavor, name, creation and destruction, credential hashing, lookup and creation, translation between flavor and GSS info in both directions, key timeout handling and a ping probe, through callbacks create, destroy, hash_cred, lookup_cred, crcreate, info2flavor, flavor2info, key_timeout and ping.

Credential operations comprise a flavor name with initialization and destruction, matching, marshaling, refresh, validation, request wrapping and response unwrapping, key timeout, acceptor stringification and a reencode predicate, through callbacks cr_init, crdestroy, crmatch, crmarshal, crrefresh, crvalidate, crwrap_req, crunwrap_resp, crkey_timeout, crstringify_acceptor and crneed_reencode.
Credential reference acquisition returns the same pointer after incrementing its count when the input is non null and already referenced, otherwise it returns null without side effects.
A cache entry header carries hash linkage in cache_list, an expiry instant in expiry_time, a last refresh instant in last_refresh, a reference count in ref and a flag word in flags.

Cache entries use four flag states: valid data present, negative result, upcall pending without reply, and cleaned from cache. Pending entries record when the upcall was sent while other entries record when the update arrived.
New cache items awaiting confirmation use an expiry interval of 120 seconds. A sentinel value 0x7FFFFFFF represents never expiring.

A cache registry carries owner, hash sizing and table with a hash lock, a name, and callbacks for release, upcall, notification, request formatting, parsing, display, missing listener warning, allocation, flushing, matching, initialization and update. Internal state tracks flush horizon, sibling linkage, next check time, entry count, pending requests and readers with a queue lock, wait queue and sequence number, writer count with last close and warning times, a filesystem location that is either procfs or pipefs, and a network namespace.

A lookup blocking description carries a defer callback and a maximum wait in jiffies. A deferred waiter carries hash linkage, FIFO linkage, the awaited cache item, an owner used for bulk discard, and a revisit callback receiving a congestion indication.

Two helpers convert between monotonic boot relative seconds and wall clock seconds using the recorded boot time, one reporting seconds since boot and the other shifting a boot relative value to wall clock.

Reference helpers provide unconditional acquisition, acquisition that fails when the count is already zero, release through the owning detail with a hint update to the next check time when the entry is nearly unreferenced and expires early, and an expiry predicate combining absolute expiry with flush horizon for valid entries.

An entry counts as expired when its expiry instant precedes current boot relative time. Non valid entries are otherwise treated as not expired, while valid entries also expire when the detail flush horizon has reached their last refresh instant.

The cache registry provides a hash lock and a queue lock with a wait queue, alongside reference counting and RCU safe acquisition, indicating hashed lookup and channel queuing are separately synchronized.

Four text helpers consume one whitespace delimited word from a cursor and interpret it as signed integer, unsigned integer, time value, or expiry adjusted from wall clock to boot relative form. Missing words report ENOENT and malformed words report EINVAL, with the cursor advanced past consumed input.
A sysfs view of a client carries a kernel object in kobject, network namespace in net, client pointer in clnt and transport switch pointer in xprt_switch.

A client object carries a reference count, numeric identifier, global and task lists, a task identifier counter, a spinlock, an RCU protected transport pointer, procedure metadata with program and version numbers and maximum procedure, authenticator, statistics and metrics, single bit behavior flags for soft retry, soft errors, disconnect retry, retransmit timeout suppression, autobind, verbosity, shutdown and fatal unreachable handling, security parameters for transport, round trip estimator with timeout strategy plus defaults, swapper count, node name length and buffer, pipe directory state, parent linkage for clones, program descriptor, machine principal, debug and sysfs locations, a union of cl_xpi and cl_work sharing storage, a credential, connection limits, pipefs superblock and task count.
Maximum supported RPC version is four. Wire protocol version in use is two.

A program descriptor carries a name, program number, version count with version array, statistics and pipe directory name. A version descriptor carries a version number, procedure count with procedure array, and per procedure call counters.

A procedure descriptor carries a procedure number in p_proc, encode and decode callbacks in p_encode and p_decode, argument and reply header lengths in p_arglen and p_replen, a timer selector in p_timer, a statistics index in p_statidx and a name in p_name.

Client creation parameters bundle network namespace, protocol, server and source addresses with sizes, timeout strategy, server and node names, program descriptor with statistics and optional program and version overrides, authentication flavor, connection counts and flags, client name, backchannel transport, credential, connection limits, security policy and connect timeouts. A transport test hook bundles a callback with opaque data for vetting added transports.

Client creation flags occupy single bit positions: hard retry at bit zero, autobind at bit two, non privileged port at bit three, no ping at bit four, disconnect retry at bit five, quiet at bit six, infinite slots at bit seven, no idle timeout at bit eight, no retransmit timeout at bit nine, soft error at bit ten, reuse port at bit eleven, connected at bit twelve and fatal unreachable at bit thirteen.

A reply is expected exactly when the task message references a procedure whose decode callback is present. Connection closing forces a disconnect of the task transport when one is attached, otherwise it does nothing.

Diagnostic helpers emit facility scoped messages when debugging for that facility is enabled, otherwise they compile to no output. One variant assumes RCU protection is managed by the caller while another acquires it internally. Disabled builds replace all tests and prints with constant false and no output. Output goes to tracing in one configuration and to standard logging in another.
In this configuration debug filesystem lifecycle for the module and per client and per transport registration are no operations returning no value.
A security context handle carries a mechanism reference in mech_type, an opaque mechanism specific identifier in internal_ctx_id, and slack and alignment sizing hints in slack and align.
Absence of a buffer is represented by a zero net object, absence of a context by a null pointer, and default quality of protection by zero. Object identifier storage allows at most thirty two bytes.

An object identifier carries a length with fixed capacity data. GSS selection info bundles such an identifier with quality and service values. A pseudoflavor descriptor bundles pseudoflavor, quality, service, names, a domain reference and a data touch flag.

A mechanism descriptor carries list linkage, owner, object identifier, name, operation vector, a count with pseudoflavor array, and an upcall encryption type list. Operations provide context import, integrity checksum generation and verification, message wrapping and unwrapping, and context deletion.
Overlapping tail members alias the same bytes as the whole object prefix, so writes through one view are visible in the other and sizing must respect the flexible member offset to avoid truncation.

Asynchronous stop queuing uses caller supplied storage that must outlive the queued work, and targeting another processor only warns without queuing, so callers cannot rely on remote execution in this configuration.

Cache release updates a shared next check hint without additional ordering shown, and RCU acquisition can fail concurrently with release while expiry depends on both absolute time and flush horizon, so callers must handle null returns and revalidate after lookup.
